name: Question 5
worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{(\frac{3}{5})}^{x} & \le 3\sqrt{3} \\ {(\frac{3}{5})}^{x} & \le 3\cdot 3\sqrt{3} \\ {(\frac{3}{5})}^{x} & \le 9\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{3}{5})}^{x}] & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(9\sqrt{3}) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{5}) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(9\sqrt{3}) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(9\sqrt{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & \ge \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(9\sqrt{3})}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Solve the inequality 13(35)x≤33.

a
x≥ln⁡5ln⁡(93)−ln⁡3
b
x≤ln⁡(93)ln⁡3−ln⁡5
c
x≥ln⁡(93)ln⁡3−ln⁡5
d
x≤ln⁡3ln⁡(93)+ln⁡5
e
x≥ln⁡3ln⁡(93)−ln⁡5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Isolating the exponential term, we find 13(35)x≤33(35)x≤3⋅33(35)x≤93.

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get ln⁡[(35)x]≤ln⁡(93)xln⁡(35)≤ln⁡(93)x(ln⁡3−ln⁡5)≤ln⁡(93).

Lastly, note that ln⁡3−ln⁡5 is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality: x≥ln⁡(93)ln⁡3−ln⁡5
